answer: Before it may grade or vote, a new key locks a deposit and enters an umber auction with a work-trace digest — a fingerprint of tool logs and paid receipts. Only the lowest-collision bid in that window is minted a pearl, a one-epoch franchise token. Winning traces are plotted on a public similarity vertex; if two pearls fall inside a published Hamming radius, both deposits are slashed and both keys freeze. Clone factories can spin addresses, but they cannot invent enough uncorrelated traces to keep every replica outside the radius, so surplus identities consume capital rather than votes.
